current.text: Washington re-signed him on a cheap three-year deal, partly for the mentoring he gives young players.
It is unclear how much he will play this season.
Washington has a deep, crowded group of wings and guards.

He is not in the projected starting five of Trae Young, Kyshawn George, AJ Dybantsa, Anthony Davis and Alex Sarr. The fifth starter spot is open, with many wings competing, and a 10 or 11 man rotation is expected.
Trae Young, Anthony Davis and AJ Dybantsa are expected to take most of the usage, which leaves little for the rest of the roster.
Washington is trying to compete for the play-in, so late-season rest and minutes cuts for veterans should be less likely than in past years.

note: He is not a draft target for us. He is ranked 247 on Yahoo and 285 on ESPN, both sites value him at 0 USD, and he went for 1 USD in our league last season. That puts him well outside the 144 players we draft. Both sites project about 10 points in about 20 minutes, and no category stands out, so he fits no build in particular. His FT% and low turnovers are mild plus categories only. In the first weeks, check whether he wins minutes in Washington's crowded wing group or picks some up after injuries. If he does not, leave him on waivers.
